articles.title: Bob Myers Reveals Message to Jaylen Brown After 76ers-Celtics Trade, Emphasizes Leadership
articles.summary: Bob Myers, the President of HBSE Sports, revealed his message to Jaylen Brown after the Philadelphia 76ers added the five-time All-Star via trade from the Boston Celtics in July.
articles.body:
Bob Myers, the President of HBSE Sports, revealed his message to Jaylen Brown after the Philadelphia 76ers added the five-time All-Star via trade from the Boston Celtics in July.

Myers made his remarks to former NBA superstars Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady on The Cousins podcast .

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

The Philadelphia 76ers have made the playoffs eight of the last nine years but haven't advanced past the Eastern Conference semifinals. Last year's team upset the Boston Celtics in the first round of the playoffs but lost to the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks in the second round.

Philadelphia went all-in this offseason, however, trading Paul George and four draft picks for Brown and later adding LeBron James via free agency. They join a formidable trio featuring 2022-23 NBA MVP Joel Embiid, All-NBA Third Team member Tyrese Maxey and unanimous All-Rookie First Team member VJ Edgecombe.

It's a formidable lineup for a 76ers team searching for its first Eastern Conference title since 2001 and its first NBA championship since 1983.

Philadelphia has certainly added championship experience and veteran leadership to the team. James is entering his 24th NBA season and has 10 NBA Finals appearances and four NBA championships. Brown has played 10 seasons, with a pair of NBA Finals trips, six Eastern Conference Finals appearances and one title. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, a two-time NBA champion, is aboard as well and will be a key player off the bench.

It's clear from Myers' remarks that he valued Brown's past success and the leadership he can bring to the table. The same could go for James and KCP as well, as Philadelphia looks to finally take that next step.

articles.title: Juancho Hernangómez: "La selección pinta muy bien para los próximos años"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño, segundo capitán de la selección, protagonista en Radio MARCA
articles.summary: El madrileño, segundo capitán de la selección, protagonista en Radio MARCA
articles.body: Juancho Hernangómez vuelve a 'La Familia'. El alero madrileño afronta los importantes encuentros de clasificación para el Mundial 2027 ante Portugal y Grecia como segundo capitán del conjunto español y ejerciendo de padrino de los nuevos talentos que vienen como Aday Mara, Hugo González o Baba Miller. Desde la concentración de Zaragoza, atendió la llamada de 'El Programa de Ortega'. "Muchas ganas de jugar con ellos, ya les conocía desde hace años y ver cómo ha ido su progresión...vienen con muchas ganas y creo que pinta muy bien la selección para los próximos años, tienen mucho talento, son buenas personas, compiten", apuntó sobre los primeros días de preparación. El pasado Eurobasket, en el que España no consiguió pasar de la fase de grupos, supuso el fin de la era Scariolo y el nacimiento de la nueva generación con el concurso de Sergio De Larrea, Santi Aldama o Mario Saint Supery. Juancho no vivió sus mejores días en Chipre, una experiencia que le ha ayudado a crecer y mejorar. "Se pasa mal, pero no es de los peores momentos que he tenido en mi carrera deportiva. De todo se aprende. Creo que fue un campeonato para aprender. Yo tuve la suerte de llegar y tocar el cielo y ganar, pero cuando perdimos hablando con Rudy y Llull me decían que lo difícil es eso, es empezar, aprender, que los jóvenes vayan cogiendo experiencia...no pasa nada, de todo se aprende, las experiencias malas hay que vivirlas y para disfrutar las buenas hay que pasarlo mal. Hemos aprendido de ello y ahora tenemos un nuevo reto", comentó. Los hermanos Hernangómez ejercen desde el pasado verano como capitanes de la selección. Tomando el testigo de Sergio Llull y Rudy Fernández y con la misión de seguir manteniendo intactos los valores que identifican al baloncesto español. "Sigue siendo un sueño, para mi familia y para mí venir con la selección siempre ha sido nuestra prioridad, ganar con la selección ha sido lo más bonito que nos ha pasado en nuestra vida deportiva y no lo cambio por nada. Para nosotros sigue siendo especial, vengo con la misma ilusión de siempre y seguiré viniendo siempre que el seleccionador quiera. Sigo enamorado del baloncesto, sigo enamorado de jugar con mi hermano y es un sueño poder hacerlo en cualquier equipo", valoró. Juancho Hernangómez regresó hace tres temporadas a Europa procedente de la NBA. Recaló en el Panathinaikos de Atenas, que había configurado un proyecto de élite con Ataman en el banquillo para volver a la cima europea. Al madrileño le costó arrancar, pero desde el primer día es un ídolo en la ciudad y en la afición y acaba de renovar hasta 2031 pese a tener ofertas. "He encontrado un sitio donde soy muy feliz, la manera en la que viven el baloncesto...fue un primer año muy duro, pero lo ganamos todo y cuando ganas allí es historia. Me siento muy querido y apreciado. Que te quieran al final siempre es bueno, tenía un año más de contrato, sí que tenía ofertas de otros equipos y creo que Panathinaikos me iba a dejar salir y creo que lo mejor era mi continuidad allí a largo plazo, sintiéndome muy querido por la afición, el dueño y el entrenador y es una decisión que me ha gustado", contó. Desde la próxima semana se pondrá a las órdenes de la leyenda Zeljko Obradovic, que más de una década después, ha regresado al club ateniense para seguir agrandando su palmarés. Tendrá a su disposición a Juancho y a un auténtico equipazo para aspirar a todo. "Es la presión que vivimos en Panathinaikos, fichamos a lo mejor de lo mejor y no nos vale con llegar a una final, hay que ir a por títulos y ellos lo viven así, apostar fuerte por lo mejor que haya y ganar. No tenemos otra opción. Han traído a Obradovic, que es una leyenda, ha ganado 6 veces allí la Euroliga y tengo muchas ganas de aprender de él, hablé con él antes de mi renovación. A mí me guata aprender de los mejores". El alero se formó y creció en Movistar Estudiantes, con el que debutó y se convirtió en uno de los mejores aleros de la ACB. Su rendimiento le valió el salto a la NBA, pero el madrileño sueña con un final de carrera en 'casa'. "Yo siempre he dicho que me gustaría volver a Estudiantes y retirarme dónde empezó todo, pero al final las vidas cambian mucho. Claro que es un final soñado, pero nunca me esperaba jugar en Grecia y sentirme tan querido", finalizó.

articles.title: Hailey Van Lith Lands New WNBA Contract as Sun Make Roster Moves Ahead of FIBA World Cup
articles.summary: Hailey Van Lith will get another chance to prove herself in the WNBA this week.
articles.body:
Hailey Van Lith will get another chance to prove herself in the WNBA this week.

The Connecticut Sun announced Wednesday that Van Lith signed an "upgraded" seven-day contract with Leila Lacan set to fulfill her FIBA World Cup obligations for France.

Van Lith was the 11th overall pick in the 2025 WNBA draft after her tremendous college career and figured to be a serviceable player for years to come, but she's struggled to find her place in the league early on.

Sky Ban Enes Kanter Freedom from Home Games (AP)

After a disappointing rookie year with the Chicago Sky that was marred by a nagging ankle injury, Van Lith was waived by the team this May. The Sun picked her up off waivers the same day she was cut by the Sky.

Connecticut waived her a few weeks after picking her up, but she was brought back on a developmental contract in late May. She reportedly had other options in free agency but opted to stay with the Sun because she thought it was better for her overall growth as a player.

Van Lith has made 16 appearances with Connecticut this year, putting up 5.3 points, 1.9 assists and 1.0 rebounds per game in just over 14 minutes per contest.

The seven-day contract should be a good opportunity for Van Lith to show what she can do before the season ends. Considering Lacan was a starter who played nearly 30 minutes a game, Van Lith should get plenty of playing time.

She'll also have the chance to play without much pressure since the Sun are 10-27 and have already been eliminated from playoff contention. If Van Lith can provide valuable minutes off the bench, it could lead to another opportunity this offseason.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Fever vs. Sky Becomes Most-Watched WNBA Regular-Season Game in Nearly 3 Decades
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever made WNBA broadcast history during last Sunday's victory over DiJonai Carrington and the Chicago Sky.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever made WNBA broadcast history during last Sunday's victory over DiJonai Carrington and the Chicago Sky.

A total audience delivery of 3.31 million viewers tuned in to watch Clark scored 37 points in the Fever's 113-90 win, according to NBC Sports .

That marked the WNBA regular season's most-watched game since 1997 and the third most-watched game of all time, according to the network.

Sky Ban Enes Kanter Freedom from Home Games (AP)

The record for the most-watched WNBA regular-season game stands at 5.04 million total viewers from when the New York Liberty and Los Angeles Sparks opened the league's inaugural season on NBC in June 1997.

The second-most watched regular-season game stands at 3.59 million viewers, also from the 1997 opening weekend, according to NBC Sports.

Sunday's broadcast peaked at 3.82 million viewers who watched the Fever set a franchise record with 18 three-pointers, including eight from Clark and six from Kelsey Mitchell.

The game marked the WNBA's second NBC primetime broadcast of the season following a July 12 game featuring the Fever and Las Vegas Aces.

The Fever/Aces game averaged a total audience delivery of 2.64 million viewers to make it the second most-watched game of the season, according to NBC Sports .

NBC Sports has so far averaged a total audience delivery of 1.75 million viewers for seven WNBA games aired on NBC and Peacock this season, the network reported.

The WNBA playoffs tip off Sept. 27. Semifinal and Finals coverage will be provided on NBC and Peacock as well as Disney Networks and USA Network, according to the league .

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom sends letter to WNBA requesting review of Sky ejection incident, full ticket refund
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom sent a letter to the WNBA demanding answers after security removed him from his courtside seat during a Chicago Sky game.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: Enes Kanter Freedom is demanding answers from the WNBA after security removed him from his courtside seat during Sunday’s game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena. Freedom attended the game wearing a shirt advocating for the protection of women’s sports, days after announcing his intention to enter the WNBA Draft as a form of protest. During the third quarter, Sky guard Natasha Cloud crossed the court and confronted Freedom as he sat near the baseline. In a letter sent to WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert, Freedom requested an explanation for his removal and accused the league of applying its policies selectively. Freedom called the ejection an "apparent selective enforcement of League and arena policies that raises serious concerns of viewpoint discrimination," according to the letter obtained by OutKick. The former NBA first-round pick also disputed claims from Chicago Sky co-owner Nadia Rawlinson and nearby spectators that he instigated the confrontation with Cloud. "Late in the third quarter, Chicago Sky player Natasha Cloud turned from the court, approached my seat, and began yelling, cursing, and pointing in my direction," Freedom wrote. "Security and Sky personnel intervened, and I was subsequently escorted from the arena." Freedom argued that the league appeared to apply a double standard because Cloud had not been publicly reprimanded or punished for her actions. SKY COACH PRAISES NATASHA CLOUD AFTER HEATED VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH ENES KANTER FREEDOM "According to the WNBA, any physical or verbal altercation with a fan is treated as conduct detrimental to the game," Freedom wrote. "The WNBA Office holds the authority to issue heavy fines or multi-game suspensions for players who cross the line into berating or cursing at spectators. Yet Ms. Cloud’s conduct of yelling, swearing, and pointing at a spectator (me) appears to have escaped any accountability and was, in fact, defended by her coach." Freedom also disputed the contention that his own conduct warranted removal from the arena. "Meanwhile, I remained fully aware that I could not step onto the court and ensured my presence and expression complied with applicable standards," the letter states. "In other words, I followed your rules." Freedom further argued that security failed to follow the WNBA’s stated process for addressing alleged fan misconduct. WNBA ADMITS SECURITY IN ATLANTA WAS WRONG TO MAKE FANS COVER SHIRTS AT DREAM-FEVER GAME "According to the WNBA Fan Code of Conduct, a spectator should be issued a warning for any alleged violation before being forced to leave the game," Freedom wrote. "I received no such warning prior to my ejection." The letter repeatedly alleged that Freedom received unfair treatment because of his public advocacy and the message displayed on his shirt. "The circumstances of my removal only further highlight a pattern and practice of the League applying its rules unfairly," Freedom wrote. "For example, why did arena personnel believe my ejection was warranted while Ms. Cloud appears to have escaped any accountability for clearly violating League rules against the use of profanity and insults directed at fans?" Freedom specifically questioned whether his advocacy "for defending the integrity of women’s sports" or his announcement that he intended to enter the WNBA Draft played a role in the decision. "I should not be treated differently because the League, its players, or personnel disagree with my viewpoint," Freedom wrote. "The timing and circumstances of my removal beg a variety of questions: Did my WNBA Draft announcement, prior communications with the League, public advocacy for women’s sports, or the message displayed on my shirt play a role in the decision to eject me?" Freedom also connected his removal to other recent controversies involving spectators who expressed opposition to allowing transgender athletes to compete in women’s sports. "On July 28, spectators outside the Seattle Storm v. Indiana Fever game were treated differently based on their viewpoints," Freedom wrote. "While supporters of women’s sports were told they could not rally on the raised platform outside the arena, transgender activists were allowed to do so." "Next, on August 16, spectators at an Atlanta Dream v. Indiana Fever game were instructed to cover shirts supporting women’s sports that were like mine, while allowing pro-transgender shirts to remain. Although the WNBA subsequently acknowledged that the intervention ‘should not have happened,’ it was no more than a week later that I was removed from the August 23 WNBA game wearing a shirt expressing a similar viewpoint." Freedom argued that those incidents "raise significant questions about the WNBA’s application of its own rules depending on the perceived viewpoints of its spectators." "It goes without saying that when I purchase a ticket to attend a WNBA game, I expect that I will not be discriminated against based on my viewpoint," Freedom wrote. Freedom requested "a written response within five business days" addressing five specific demands: "1. Identify the policy, rule, directive, or instruction relied upon in treating certain spectators, including me, differently when we express a viewpoint that appears unpopular with the WNBA; "2. Identify whether the decision to eject me was made or requested by WNBA personnel, Chicago Sky personnel, Wintrust Arena personnel, security personnel, or another individual or entity; "3. Confirm whether Ms. Cloud’s conduct has been or will be reviewed under any League policy governing player interactions with fans, including rules governing altercations that require player suspension, and state what accountability, if any, she, her team, and management will face; "4. Provide a full refund of the cost of my courtside tickets; and "5. Preserve all materials relating to this incident, including relevant video footage, incident or security reports, communications concerning my attendance or removal, communications referring to my WNBA Draft announcement or public advocacy for women’s sports, and any applicable policies or event-day directives." Freedom is asking the league to identify who ordered his removal, explain the rule he allegedly violated and determine whether Cloud’s conduct merits a formal review. articles.title: New Steph Curry Rumors Update Warriors Contract Extension Talks Ahead of Eligibility Date
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star point guard Stephen Curry is reportedly expected to receive a new payday soon.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star point guard Stephen Curry is reportedly expected to receive a new payday soon.

Curry becomes eligible for a contract extension on Saturday, and ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that team sources confirmed that he and the Warriors "are expected to engage with a mutual desire to keep Curry with the Warriors for the entirety of his career."

Curry is set to make $62.6 million this season in the final year of his previous deal, and he's eligible for an extension of up to two years and $136.7 million. Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy expressed confidence earlier this month that the two-time NBA MVP won't be going anywhere anytime soon.

"Ultimately it's his call, his decision, whether that's allowing his contract to run out and move on," Dunleavy said. "Look, if he comes to me and wants to be moved, [controlling owner] Joe [Lacob] and I will talk it through. We wouldn't love it. But he's earned the right to do what he wants. But as far as the messaging or any idea that he'd be anywhere else, that's not a thing we're looking at or he's looking at."

The Warriors have had a relatively quiet offseason after failing to land any of the big-name players they pursued. Golden State focused on bolstering its depth over the last few weeks, and the team signed veteran power forward Georges Niang and reserve guard Brandon Williams to one-year deals on Wednesday.

While the Warriors aren't expected to contend for a championship this year, Curry's loyalty to the team likely will ensure that he will remain the face of the franchise for the foreseeable future.

articles.title: Draymond Green Questions If Klay Thompson Will Fit with 'Heat Culture' After Signing Contract
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green weighed in on former teammate Klay Thompson signing with the Miami Heat following his departure from the Dallas Mavericks.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green weighed in on former teammate Klay Thompson signing with the Miami Heat following his departure from the Dallas Mavericks.

"I found it interesting when I saw they said, 'Klay going to Miami,'" Green said on The Draymond Green Show (0:36 mark). "I was like, 'Oh, that Heat Culture thing.' I don't know how that's going to work for Klay because Klay moves to the beat of his own drum. It's no maliciousness to it, it's just who Klay is and I want to see how that fits into 'Heat Culture' stuff. And so I'm looking forward to seeing how that happens."

Michael Jordan expected to leave media role

Thompson agreed to a two-year, $11.5 million contract with Miami on Sunday.

Green and Thompson were previously teammates on the Warriors from 2012-24, winning four championships together while playing alongside Stephen Curry.

Thompson has been known for his laid-back personality and affinity for being on his boat . He was reportedly late for his introductory press conference with Miami after getting stuck in traffic.

Meanwhile, Heat president Pat Riley has been a proponent of the "Heat Culture" philosophy. The hard-working, professional mindset has been a staple of the organization and featured on a jersey in the past.

Thompson revealed that he was excited to join the culture of his new organization

"We were talking about the conditioning test last night," Thompson said Tuesday, per Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel . "So I'm happy I've got five weeks to really prepare. I've got to get my treadmill back operating. But I'm really excited just to be pushed on a fitness level that I know will be so beneficial for me for this next season.

"A lot of players warn me about how tough it is, but I like hard stuff like that. I've been through harder things. Coming back from those injuries was harder than any conditioning drill or game I had to play. In a weird way, those injuries prepared me for uncomfortable feelings and tough times. Now I take it head on and embrace them."

Thompson is coming off a 2025-26 season with Dallas in which he averaged 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game while shooting 39.3 percent from the field and 38.3 percent from three-point territory.

The high profile couple recently celebrated their foundation celebrating seven years of changing lives in Oakland and now, they have marked a new achievement.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat. Learn & Play, make a major difference in bridging the literacy gap in OaklandJust a few days ago, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat. articles.title: The one NBA ROTY edge Grizzlies' Cameron Boozer has vs. Darryn Peterson, AJ Dybantsa
articles.summary: ESPN has Grizzlies' Cam Boozer winning the 2027 NBA ROTY over Jazz's Darryn Peterson and Wizards' AJ Dybantsa.
articles.body:
A good barometer of an NBA Draft Class' depth is how close the Rookie of the Year race is. Plenty of names are in the mix to take home the award, but about five stand out. Among them, Cameron Boozer of the Memphis Grizzlies is the favorite to win the award, per ESPN's Summer Forecast. What edge does he have over Darryn Peterson of the Utah Jazz and AJ Dybantsa of the Washington Wizards ? Let's break it down.

Grizzlies' Boozer edges out Dybantsa, Peterson for NBA ROTY race in ESPN's Summer Forecast

Heading into the 2026 NBA Draft, there was no clear order for who would land in the top five, but a short list of names was already guaranteed to do so. Those same players will now have to duke it out for the NBA ROTY race. Five names stand above the rest: Memphis Grizzlies' Cameron Boozer, Sacramento Kings ' Darius Acuff Jr., Chicago Bulls ' Caleb Wilson, Utah Jazz 's Darryn Peterson, and Washington Wizards ' AJ Dybantsa.

How do all of these NBA ROTY candidates stack up against each other? ESPN forecasted one slim favorite, with an ingrained edge that his team has and no other squad offers.

Notably, the frontrunners are the same people who were drafted first, second, third, and fourth overall. Acuff Jr. is also the only one with the highest odds outside of the top five picks to land on the list.

Among all of them, why does Boozer have a five-point difference that sets him apart?

It all has to do with the Grizzlies and the minutes they can afford him so he can develop.

"These players all landed in situations that should be beneficial from an early usage and minutes standpoint, but it's Boozer who should have the biggest role of the three, with Memphis likely to orient its operation around him for the foreseeable future as it needs an offensive player who can shoulder a scoring load and connect teammates. On paper, he looks like the slight favorite," ESPN declared.

Boozer will be handed the keys to the Grizzlies, a luxury that his other NBA ROTY competitors will not be afforded. This is because Ja Morant left for the Portland Trail Blazers , and the Grizzlies are focusing on their young guys rather than being forced to compete.

Peterson, for instance, will likely be benched often if his performances don't pan out, making way for guys like Ace Bailey , Keyonte George , and Lauri Markkanen . The same goes with Dybantsa, who is pressured to perform immediately alongside Trae Young and Anthony Davis for a postseason spot in a cutthroat Eastern Conference.

Wilson might have the most leeway in development, which could threaten Boozer's NBA ROTY win. Even then, he cannot be as ball-dominant as he was back with the UNC Tar Heels. This is because guys like Norman Powell , Josh Giddey , Matas Buzelis , Patrick Williams , and Rob Dillingham have something to prove to the Bulls organization.

The Grizzlies immediately get to start Boozer at the power forward spot ahead of guys like Taylor Hendricks and GG Jackson . Other players on their roster also don't need any sort of heliocentrism to be effective. Boozer gets complemented well with the two-way prowess of teammates like Scotty Pippen Jr. , Cedric Coward , Jerami Grant , and Zach Edey .

When all of these considerations are put into place, it's not hard to see why the Grizzlies will get their third NBA ROTY winner after Pau Gasol and Ja Morant. Will any unseen contender step up to usurp expectations and beat Boozer by the end of the year?

articles.title: Draymond Green Calls Out 'Bulls--t' Narratives Around Klay Thompson's Heat Contract
articles.summary: Draymond Green believes sports media is setting up former teammate Klay Thompson for failure after the sharp-shooter joined the Miami Heat.
articles.body:
Draymond Green believes sports media is setting up former teammate Klay Thompson for failure after the sharp-shooter joined the Miami Heat.

"I don't like how everybody is trying to act like 'oh it's Klay Thompson! Klay to the Heat!' Like this is Klay from 2018," the Golden State Warriors forward said on his podcast. "The reason I don't like it is because I feel like everybody is trying to set Klay up for failure. I'm going to say it right here right now. Let's stop acting like it's 2017 Klay going to Miami.

"I wish sports media would speak on it more like when Ray Allen went to Miami. That's the role I'd expect Klay to play. Don't try to set my brother up like you about to get the 2017 Klay so the moment you don't, you all can bash him. That's bulls--t. He's going into year 16 of his career. And we obviously know the injuries that he's faced. Yes he is going to provide shooting because he can shoot the lights out the ball. … But don't try to build it up like 'oh man look what happened' so y'all can tear him down."

Green defending Thompson is anything but a surprise, as they won four championships together with the Warriors.

His comments about tempering expectations are also fair. Thompson is 36 years old, has suffered multiple significant injuries during his career and was moved into a bench role last season for the Dallas Mavericks as he averaged a career-low 11.7 points per game.

Frankly, Thompson isn't going to be the Splash Brothers version of himself who could take over games with his scoring during his peak with the Warriors. He was a perfect complement to Stephen Curry on the offensive side and was also a lockdown defender at his best.

Still, it is easy to look at his fit with the Heat and believe in his ability to make an impact.

Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are going to generate the majority of defensive attention from opponents, which should lead to plenty of open looks from their teammates. Thompson is better suited than almost anyone in NBA history to knock down those open looks from the outside.

And Green acknowledged as much by saying Thompson will shoot at an incredible level until he is 60 years old.

But that doesn't mean he is going to be the same player he was when he was a five-time All-Star and two-time All-NBA selection in Golden State.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark helps Fever deliver WNBA's largest regular-season TV audience in 29 years
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's 37-point performance against the Chicago Sky drew 3.31 million viewers, the most-watched WNBA regular season game since 1997.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark didn’t need Enes Kanter Freedom or DiJonai Carrington to turn Fever-Sky into appointment TV Sunday night. Her presence has made every Indiana Fever game must-watch television. Still, the nearly 3.5 million people who watched on NBC and Peacock got more than a typical Fever game. First, there was Carrington spending two weeks making the rematch personal. Then, there was Kanter bringing the WNBA’s women’s-sports debate directly courtside. WHO IS DIJONAI CARRINGTON? WNBA STAR WHO SMACKED SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM, GOT EJECTED AND BLAMED 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' Indiana’s 113-90 win averaged 3.31 million viewers and peaked at 3.82 million, making it the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since opening weekend in 1997, the league’s inaugural season, and the third-most-watched WNBA regular-season game ever. Caitlin Clark drives the WNBA audience Clark had already shown what she does with a national television window. Indiana’s July 12 game against the defending champion Las Vegas Aces averaged 2.64 million viewers across NBC and Peacock. That's been a theme throughout the season. Clark's popularity even had rival networks arguing about which one aired the most-watched WNBA game of the season last month. Clark and the Fever had already broken all-time WNBA viewership records on CBS, ESPN, ION and Prime Video with the Aug. 16 Fever-Dream game on ESPN also becoming the largest cable audience in league history. CAITLIN CLARK HELPS WNBA SHATTER ANOTHER TV RATINGS RECORD AS FEVER-DREAM DRAWS MASSIVE AUDIENCE NBC deserves credit for putting Indiana in a rare Sunday-night primetime spot. But it can’t manufacture the appetite. Fever games are appointment viewing, and Clark is the reason. DiJonai Carrington made the rematch personal Carrington made sure this game came with more heat than a normal late-season matchup. On Aug. 8, she was ejected for a Flagrant Foul 2 after blasting Fever guard Sophie Cunningham in the face while Cunningham attempted a fast-break layup. Afterward, Carrington tagged the Fever in a Threads post reading "WHITE PRIVILEGE," then followed it with "8/23" on X. She’d put the rematch on the calendar herself. Clark and Carrington already had history, too. In 2024, Carrington poked Clark in the eye during a playoff game and before that mocked Clark for, in Carrington's view, flopping. The ejection, the accusation, the history and the date made the next meeting must-see TV before a single second ran off the clock. Then Clark delivered. She scored 37 points, went 8 of 12 from 3-point range and dished out 10 assists. When she drilled a three over Carrington, the two had a brief exchange. Meanwhile, Carrington scored just 7 points on 3 of 11 shooting and went 0 for 3 from distance. Enes Kanter Freedom brought the women’s-sports fight courtside Then there was Kanter. After joining a small rally in support of Cunningham before the game, Kanter took a baseline seat wearing a shirt that read, "WOMAN noun. adult human female." Kanter didn’t wander into Wintrust Arena with a provocative shirt with zero context. In the weeks after ESPN published Cunningham’s comments about protecting girls and women from competing against biological men, Kanter claimed he was declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft. He argued that self-identification should be enough under the league’s rules. The WNBA’s CBA says only women can play, but it doesn’t define the term or lay out separate rules for gender identity or sex assigned at birth. Kanter was trying to force the league to confront that gap. Late in the third quarter, Chicago guard Natasha Cloud scored a layup and started yelling at Kanter. Cloud is one of the WNBA’s most outspoken left-wing political voices. Following Cloud's outburst, Kanter put his arms out and walked onto the court toward Cloud before he was escorted out by security. The Sky later banned him from the team's home games. Kanter and Cloud certainly weren't the reason 3.31 million people tuned in. The interaction happened too late in the game to receive that credit. But he put the league’s women’s-sports fight in front of the people who were already watching and created an immediate social media firestorm that certainly didn't hurt viewership for folks who might have seen that and then tuned in for the final quarter. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP So, the game started with Caitlin Clark, which practically guarantees a seven-figure TV audience for the WNBA. Then you add in the Carrington angle and the Kanter controversy and the recipe for a record-setting TV audience was in place. And that's exactly what happened.

articles.title: Chicago Sky owner opens up on Enes Kanter Freedom ejection, makes analogy to shooting a gun
articles.summary: Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter compared Enes Kanter Freedom's ejection from Wintrust Arena to shooting a gun, saying certain threats don't get warnings.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: Chicago Sky principal owner Michael Alter addressed the team's decision to eject and ban Enes Kanter Freedom from Wintrust Arena in an exclusive interview on Wednesday. When asked why Freedom was not given a warning, Alter made the analogy that someone would not receive a warning for shooting a gun at someone before being punished. Alter announced on Tuesday that Kanter was banned after his ejection from Sunday's game against the Fever, as the team determined that he was "a threat." Alter said Wednesday the determination that Freedom was a "threat" was a when he "took a step towards the court." "That's when he became a potential threat," Alter said. "We had league security, we had arena security, we had Indiana Fever, Chicago Sky security, Chicago Police Department, all of them were there. All of them acted immediately. All of them, you know, it was the quickest decision I've ever seen in someone being ejected from a game." ENES KANTER FREEDOM, DEEMED TO HAVE ‘THE POTENTIAL TO BE A THREAT,’ RESPONDS TO SKY OWNER'S COMMENTS OutKick reached out to Chicago police for a request for comment. Freedom has since argued he should have been given a warning before his ejection in a letter to the WNBA. The WNBA fan code does not state that fans are entitled to a warning before ejection. When asked why Freedom was not given a warning before his ejection, Alter said "He wasn’t given a warning because certain threats don’t get warnings. "To use an extreme example, uh, when you, when you shoot a gun at someone, you don't get a warning, 'Don't do that again.' It, it's, you know, your action doesn't deserve a warning." Alter acknowledged that he does not know if Freedom actually stepped on the court. Freedom has said he did not step on the court. The WNBA Fan Code states that fans who attempt to enter the court will be immediately ejected. Footage shows Freedom stepping toward the court, before a security guard promptly comes over and stops him from going any further. "The security were there to stop him ... The Indiana Fever guy was right there. He was right in front of him. The guy from the arena, Monterey, was right there. It took a second for Chicago's guys to go to get there, but they got there pretty damn fast," Alter said, later adding, "I can’t tell you what his intent was beyond his actions. I don't know what was in his head, OK. Neither do you. And if he tells you what's his intent based on the other things he's told you, you have to know he is completely unreliable." Freedom has alleged that the confrontation began after he cheered for Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. According to Freedom, Cloud turned toward him and said, "She’s not going to sleep with you," before later cursing at him. "Was she part of the confrontation? Yes, she was," Alter said. "They were going back and forth, so that is correct." When asked whether the Sky had determined that Cloud violated any rules or planned to discipline her, Alter said, "There was not." Alter said he had not spoken to either participant about that allegation. "I’ve not talked to Natasha nor Mr. Freedom about it, but I have talked to several people who were sitting right there and did not have a stake in the matter," Alter said. "These are people who did not know each other. They didn’t come with each other. I spoke with them independently of each other, so they had no knowledge of what the other person told me." Alter said those spectators told him that Freedom initiated the first verbal interaction by directing basketball-related trash talk at Cloud. He said security did not intervene at that point because the comments had not crossed the line. EX-LAKERS PLAYER SPEAKS OUT IN DEFENSE OF ENES KANTER, DOUBLES DOWN AGAINST WNBA'S TRANS ISSUE "What they all shared with me was that he initiated the first verbal contact with Cloud, with doing some what I characterize as basketball trash talking," Alter said. "That was the first initial contact between Cloud and Mr. Freedom. That’s what then spiraled into the back and forth between them." Alter said the exchange included "her shouting things at him" and Freedom making "hand gestures and facial gestures" toward her. However, Alter could not provide the exact words the spectators attributed to Freedom. Alter also acknowledged that he did not have audio confirming the spectators’ accounts. "I do not have any audio," he said. But according to Alter, at least one nearby spectator offered a different perspective. A woman wearing Fever apparel who sat behind Freedom said she did not hear him say anything to Cloud before Cloud approached him, Alter said. "She was sitting behind him, contrary to whoever did write about it, said she was sitting in the same row with him or near him," Alter said. "She wasn’t. She was actually sitting behind him and a few seats down. So I believe her that she didn’t hear him say anything." Alter suggested that the woman couldn't hear it. "It would be very hard for her to hear it given where she was sitting," Alter said. "Her comment is not inconsistent with what I was told by people who were actually sitting in direct proximity." The witnesses have not been publicly identified, Alter could not provide Freedom’s alleged words and no audio has surfaced to verify either version. Alter nevertheless characterized Freedom’s claim that he did not initiate the exchange as a lie. "We now know that is a lie," Alter said. Alter also repeatedly declined to discuss whether Cloud’s actions received or would receive a separate review. When asked why the Sky had not disciplined Cloud if she approached Freedom before he stood and moved toward the court, Alter said her conduct did not affect Freedom’s responsibility for his own actions. "Her role in this has nothing to do with our decision and how we handle Mr. Freedom," Alter said. When pressed about whether Cloud was partially responsible for the overall confrontation, Alter said, "Fans have to be responsible for their own actions, period." Alter then declined to answer additional questions about Cloud. "I’m not here to talk to you about Natasha Cloud," he said. The WNBA rulebook allows officials to assess a technical foul without warning for conduct they consider detrimental to the game. It also identifies profanity and taunting as unsportsmanlike tactics. Sky coach Tyler Marsh defended Cloud after the game and described her as someone who protects her teammates and "people that need to be protected." Alter also addressed the advance notice the Sky received that Freedom would attend the game. Freedom’s manager, Hank Fetic, sent Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca a text at 2:31 p.m. Sunday that read: "Jeff, "This is Hank (Enes’ manager) i got a new number. You have always been fair to me so i figured you deserved a heads up in advance. "Enes and I will be at the sky game tonight. "Hope you are well." Pagliocca responded at 5:30 p.m., approximately 30 minutes before the scheduled tipoff: "Appreciate the text, hope you are well too." Freedom had previously characterized Pagliocca’s response as telling his manager to "enjoy the game." However, the screenshot does not include a text that said, "enjoy the game." Alter pointed to that discrepancy as one example of what he said were inaccurate statements from Freedom. "He said that he was told by our GM to enjoy the game," Alter said. "Now that you have the text, you know that’s not what he said." Pagliocca’s message acknowledged the notice and returned Fetic’s well wishes. It did not tell Freedom to "enjoy the game." Freedom's representatives have addressed the inconsistency in the text. "The text was sent by his manager and his manager paraphrased to him," Freedom's representative told OutKick. But the exchange also did not tell Freedom that he was unwelcome. Pagliocca did not instruct him to stay away, warn him about his conduct or place any special conditions on his attendance. The parties instead disagree about how to interpret Fetic’s statement that Pagliocca "deserved a heads up in advance." Alter said the Sky viewed that language as a warning that Freedom planned to create a disturbance. "When you say you deserve to know, why would you say you deserve to know?" Alter said. "That’s a clear, direct indication that be ready, trouble’s coming." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Alter argued that someone simply attending a game would ordinarily provide notice in more welcoming terms. "If you’re coming to a game to have fun, you say, ‘Hey, guess what? I’m coming. Wanted to let you know. Look forward to seeing you,’ something like that," Alter said. "You don’t say, ‘You deserve a heads up.’" But Fetic’s text did not explicitly mention trouble, a protest or an intention to provoke anyone. Alter’s interpretation rested on an inference from the wording and the surrounding circumstances rather than an express warning in the message. Alter also cited the fact that another person purchased Freedom’s ticket. He said Freedom had acknowledged that arrangement publicly and indicated that he did not want the Sky to learn about his attendance through the ticket purchase. "Most people, 99.9% of the people who come to Sky games, do not try and hide the fact that they’re coming," Alter said. However, Freedom’s manager did notify the Sky more than three hours before the scheduled start of the game. Alter argued that Freedom’s group controlled the timing of that disclosure and left the organization with limited time to prepare. "They went out of their way through the way they purchased the ticket to make sure that we didn’t find that out any sooner than they wanted us to find it out," Alter said. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS Alter said the organization informed its security personnel once it learned Freedom was coming. The Sky did not prevent him from entering or remove him because of his shirt. Alter said staff members were instructed to ignore Freedom and not "take the bait." The players, however, were not told that Freedom would be present. "Correct," Alter said when asked whether security knew but the players did not. "You probably heard me say yesterday that that was something I regret not doing." Alter said learning about Freedom’s attendance earlier might have given the Sky more time to prepare and allowed the organization to notify its players. But he said it probably would not have changed the decision to allow Freedom inside the arena. "We didn’t keep him from coming," Alter said. "Despite all these things, despite the fact that we knew his intentions were not to just do no harm, we knew very well what his intentions were." The text exchange establishes that Freedom’s manager provided advance notice and that Pagliocca acknowledged it. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP What the exchange does not establish is Freedom’s intent. Alter interpreted it as a warning of impending trouble. Freedom’s side presented it as a courtesy notice that demonstrated the group was not secretly entering the game. The language itself does not expressly resolve between those interpretations.

articles.title: DeWanna Bonner Reportedly Signs Dream Contract, Latest WNBA Standings for Angel Reese, Atlanta

The Atlanta Dream signed DeWanna Bonner as a free agent on Wednesday, according to ESPN's Alexa Philippou .

Bonner's deal is worth $116,000, per Philippou .

She opened the 2026 season as a member of the Phoenix Mercury, but agreed to a contract buyout with the team on Monday.

Bonner is now joining a Dream squad that's currently battling for positioning in the WNBA playoff picture led by star forward Angel Reese.

Meanwhile, the Mercury were eliminated from playoff contention on Saturday.

Bonner appeared in 37 contests prior to her exit from Phoenix, averaging 10.6 points, 6.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 39.4 percent from the field and 26.2 percent from three-point territory.

The 39-year-old has racked up six All-Star nods, three Sixth Player of the Year awards, two championships and two All-WNBA selections since she was selected with the No. 5 overall pick in the 2009 draft.

Bonner sits at No. 3 on the league's all-time scoring list .

With 98 career playoff games under her belt, she brings plenty of experience to a Dream squad that has struggled with depth this year.

Atlanta's bench is averaging 17.2 points per game this season, representing the second-lowest mark among all WNBA teams.

Still, the Dream have been successful largely due to a starting lineup headlined by Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard and Reese.

Reese has recorded a career-high 16.1 points to go along with 12.4 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game during her 2026 campaign. She's also shot 43.7 percent from the field.

Bonner could make her Dream debut during their next game, a matchup with the Portland Fire on Friday.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga reaches 2-year, $13 million deal to join Timberwolves after split with Hawks
articles.summary: Jonathan Kuminga was traded to the Hawks ahead of the deadline last season.
articles.body:
Jonathan Kuminga is headed to Minneapolis.

The Minnesota Timberwolves agreed to a two-year, $13 million deal to land Kuminga on Wednesday, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The move came after the Hawks officially declined Kuminga's team option in June, making him a free agent after his tumultuous exit with the Golden State Warriors last season.

Kuminga reportedly chose the Timberwolves over similar offers from the Los Angeles Lakers , Chicago Bulls and Portland Trail Blazers .

Kuminga was dealt to the Hawks ahead of the deadline last season in a deal that sent Kristaps Porziņģis to the Warriors . That ended what was a rough run for Kuminga in Golden State.

He reportedly requested a trade as soon as he was eligible to be dealt after being largely sidelined during the first half of the season. Kuminga, whom the Warriors selected with the No. 7 overall draft pick out of the G League in 2021, only appeared in 20 games for the franchise last season.

Kuminga ended up playing 16 games with the Hawks after that trade. He averaged 12.3 points and 5.3 rebounds per contest in Atlanta . The Hawks finished 46-36 and reached the playoffs for the first time under head coach Quin Snyder, but they were knocked out in the first round.

Kuminga had signed a two-year, $46.8 million deal with the Warriors ahead of the 2025-26 season with the potential out this summer.

The loss of Kuminga arrives on the heels of multiple additions to Atlanta's roster in recent weeks. Prior to the NBA Draft, the Hawks acquired forward Aaron Wiggins from the Oklahoma City Thunder in exchange for two second-round picks.

The Hawks then acquired Houston guard Kingston Flemings (Round 1, Pick 8), St. John's forward Zuby Ejiofor (Round 1, Pick 23) and North Carolina forward/center Henri Veesaar (Round 2, Pick 52) in the draft earlier this summer.

Kuminga will join a Timberwolves group that went 49-33 last season and made the playoffs for a fifth straight time under head coach Chris Finch, though they were knocked out of the postseason in the conference semifinals. He will get to slide in alongside star Anthony Edwards and new point guard LaMelo Ball.

While his time with the Hawks and Warriors wasn't very successful, Kuminga will now get the chance for a reset.

articles.summary: Bonner, 39, joins the Dream, who have already locked up a playoff spot.
articles.body:
Free agent forward DeWanna Bonner has reportedly agreed to a deal with the Atlanta Dream , per ESPN's Alexa Philippou .

The move comes after Bonner agreed to a contract buyout with the Phoenix Mercury earlier in the week. Phoenix general manager Nick U'Ren released a statement about the move, discussing how it was out of respect for the 17-year veteran.

"Because of the relationship we have with DeWanna, we worked out a buyout agreement that gives her the opportunity to chase a title in what could be her final postseason. DeWanna will always be part of the Mercury family and we wish her all the best."

"Because of the relationship we have with DeWanna, we worked out a buyout agreement that gives her the opportunity to chase a title in what could be her final postseason.

DeWanna will always be part of the Mercury family and we wish her all the best."

Bonner was drafted by the Mercury with the fifth overall pick in the 2009 WNBA Draft. She spent the first 11 years of her career in Phoenix. After stints with the Connecticut Sun and the Indiana Fever , Bonner made her return to Phoenix in 2025.

The veteran forward brings a depth of experience to the Dream roster. She has played in 572 career games and is averaging 14.3 points and 6.0 rebounds per game.

Atlanta is 25-13 at the time of the signing and has already locked up a playoff spot. The Dream are currently the fourth seed in the playoff picture, but that can change with six regular-season games to go.

The Dream have had a balanced attack this season, led by guards Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard , as well as star forward Angel Reese .

It remains to be seen how head coach Karl Smesko will deploy Bonner. She has the talent to be added to the starting lineup alongside Reese. Bonner would also be able to give Atlanta a boost off the bench for when Reese or fellow forward Naz Hillmon needs a break.

The Dream are on a four-game win streak. Bonner will get the chance to make her debut on Friday night at home against the Portland Fire if Smesko believes she is ready.

articles.title: Lakers' Top Free-Agent, Trade Targets After Jonathan Kuminga Rejects Contract Offer for Wolves Deal
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have lost the race for free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have lost the race for free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania, the Lakers offered Kuminga a starting role and a deal worth $12 million-plus per year, but he ultimately decided to go to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Having missed out on Kuminga, the Lakers will have to look elsewhere to finalize the roster. Some top free agent and trade targets for Los Angeles could be PJ Washington, De'Andre Hunter and Bruce Brown.

Washington is under contract with the Dallas Mavericks through the 2029-30 campaign, and his $19.8 million salary for the upcoming season might be a deterrent for the Lakers, but they could include a player like Jarred Vanderbilt to free up some salary cap space.

The 28-year-old is coming off a solid season in which he averaged 14.2 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.1 blocks and a steal per game. Washington plays a similar role to Kuminga as a versatile forward, but he's arguably a better option, albeit for a higher price.

It's also worth noting that Washington played alongside Luka Dončić when the Mavs reached the Finals in 2024, so there's some chemistry with the Lakers' leader.

Hunter is a possible trade candidate for the Kings as they look to shed some cap space and avoid the luxury tax, so the Lakers could land the 28-year-old for a relatively affordable price.

While he had a bit of a down year last year, Hunter shot north of 40 percent from deep during the 2024-25 campaign and would offer Dončić a sharpshooter to dish it to on the wing.

Hunter does carry a $24.9 million cap hit, though, so making a trade for him would be a bit of a risk since he wasn't at his best last year.

Brown said last December that he planned to sign with the Lakers after the Denver Nuggets' 2023 title run (h/t SI's Ryan Ward ). Now, he could have the chance to play in Los Angeles.

Brown, a free agent, would likely be a much more affordable option than Washington or Hunter, giving Los Angeles a bit more flexibility if it wants to make any other moves during the regular season.

The 30-year-old could offer solid perimeter defense and shooting off the bench behind Austin Reaves.

While the Lakers might be a bit eager to add a player before the season starts, another option could be to let the current roster play together and then decide closer to the trade deadline what exactly it needs to make a playoff run.

articles.title: Ex-ESPN host Cindy Brunson embarrasses herself trying to discredit Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Cindy Brunson defended DiJonai Carrington's clothesline on Sophie Cunningham while dismissing Caitlin Clark's historic stats as stat padding.
articles.body: We previously discussed the all-time low the sports media reached in defending DiJonai Carrington after she clotheslined Sophie Cunningham and then posted "White privilege" from the locker room following her ejection. In doing so, no one embarrassed themselves more than former ESPN broadcaster Cindy Brunson. Brunson claimed Carrington did not deserve a Flagrant 2. Instead, she argued that Cunningham should have been ejected — not the player who clotheslined her. Brunson also shared a post claiming white WNBA players benefit from "reverse DEI." ELLE DUNCAN BLAMES CAITLIN CLARK, HER FANS FOR MEDIA SMEAR CAMPAIGN WHILE IGNORING FACTS If it appeared Brunson's remarks were driven by an agenda, she later confirmed it. She said she is Team DiJonai "all day every day." "I’m team @dijonai all day every day and at most that should’ve been a flagrant 1 not an ejection," she posted on Threads. One player Brunson does not support "all day every day" is Caitlin Clark. In another bizarre Threads tangent, Brunson attempted to discredit Clark while discussing a game that did not involve the Fever. On Sunday, Clark scored 37 points on 13-of-24 shooting, including 8-of-12 from three-point range. She also had 10 assists as the Fever defeated the Sky, 113-90. Brunson wasn't impressed. She quickly argued that Clark’s performance should be discounted because the game was not competitive. "Miss me with that stat padding 37 points, on the floor up 20 w/ a minute to go BS. The 32 points in just 26 minutes was WAY more impressive from the ⭐ on the playoff team from the lone star state," Brunson posted above a story about Seattle’s game against Dallas, in which Clark did not play. Apparently, Brunson could not praise Paige Bueckers without taking a shot at Clark. Brunson later deleted the post. But she did not do so because it was personal, desperate, or demeaning. Instead, she said she removed it because it prompted "racist" and "transphobic" comments her way. Look familiar? LET'S HAVE AN HONEST CONVERSATION ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK, RACISM, AND MEDIA COWARDICE Like so many players in the WNBA, Brunson took an unprompted shot at Clark — again, she didn't even play in the game Brunson was discussing — Clark's fans defended her, and the aggressor cried racism. They all so badly want to be victims. Brunson has since continued her crusade against Clark on X. This week, Clark recorded her fifth career 30-point, 10-assist game. She now has more 30-point, 10-assist games than the rest of WNBA history combined. Every other player in league history has combined for just four. Yet Brunson was, again, not impressed by Clark's achievement. She dismissed the accomplishment as a "small sample size." Huh? Clark has accomplished something more times in fewer than three full seasons than every other player in the WNBA’s 30-year history combined. By definition, that is not a small sample size. Elsewhere, on Tuesday night, Brunson celebrated Bueckers’ 22 points and 11 assists in a — wait for it — 96-78 Wings victory. Yet there were no complaints about stat-padding due to the margin of victory this time. Why? According to Brunson, it is "different." Apparently, it is also different when Angel Reese sets records early in her career, which Brunson might call a "small sample size" if Clark were involved. "So impressive @Reese10Angel just broke a record that has stood since May of 2003 when Chamique Holdsclaw hauled in 24 rips for her Mystics vs the Shock. Reese finished w/ 26 rebounds, 18 on the defensive glass. So TUFF. #WNBA," Brunson posted this week. When users pointed out the blowout and the level of competition, the same arguments Brunson used to diminish Clark, she said those qualifications did not matter anymore. "It doesn’t matter who the competition is, she set not one, but two WNBA records tonight‼️ Plus, Smesko doesn’t use his bench much, esp w/ Bri Jones hurt. ALL of his starters were on the floor to end this game." Got that? The competition, score and playing time do not matter when it's Reese setting the record. Further, Reese actually has padded her stats throughout the season. Literally. There are videos of her team deliberately allowing her to inflate her statistics late in games. You can see and read more about that here. To be clear, Brunson does not appear as bitter or racially motivated as some of Clark and Cunningham’s most vocal detractors. In her videos, she comes across as pleasant. And yet, she has greatly damaged her credibility. Her coverage of Clark and Cunningham is so nonsensical that it looks plainly personal. Compare how she belittles the two Fever players with how she celebrates the rest of the league. It's obvious. It is pathetic. DAKICH: SPORTS MEDIA HAS CREATED AN ‘INDUSTRY’ OUT OF COMPLAINING ABOUT WHITE ATHLETES LIKE CAITLIN CLARK It is unfortunate to watch someone who has spent nearly 30 years covering the WNBA damage her credibility because she cannot control her emotions when discussing Clark and Cunningham. Brunson likely knows the WNBA well. But how can anyone view her commentary as honest moving forward when she has so clearly abandoned honesty in her recent coverage? They cannot. For those who claim White Fever fans are the reason the WNBA has become toxic, Brunson’s timeline offers a more honest explanation. She and people like her are fueling the league’s divisiveness. They have clear personal vendettas against Clark and Cunningham, then claim victimhood when others notice it. articles.title: Fever vs. Sky WNBA's most-watched regular-season game since 1997
articles.summary: A WNBA game between the Fever and Sky hit a milestone not seen since the league debuted in 1997.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever 's victory over the Chicago Sky on Aug. 23 was the highest rated WNBA game in 30 years.

NBC Sports said on Wednesday the matchup on Sunday Night Basketball averaged a Total Audience Delivery of 3.31 million viewers between NBC and Peacock, making it the most-watched regular-season game since the league's opening weekend in 1997.The game was also the third most-watched WNBA regular-season game ever. It peaked at 3.82 million viewers. Sunday's Fever vs. Sky matchup trails two games from the league's opening weekend (June 21-22, 1997): New York Liberty vs. Los Angeles Sparks (5.04 million viewers) and Charlotte Sting vs. Phoenix Mercury (3.59 million viewers)

WNBA's Rookie of the Year award winners over the years

It was the second contest in WNBA regular-season history broadcast by a network on Sunday in prime-time. The first was on July 12, when Indiana played the defending champion Las Vegas Aces . That game averaged a TAD of 2.64 million viewers and is the second most-watched WNBA game this season.

The Fever beat the Sky, 113-90, at Wintrust Arena in Chicago on Sunday. Caitlin Clark led the way with 37 points, including a career-best eight 3-pointers, and 10 assists. Kelsey Mitchell added 30 points, four assists, two steals and a block.Chicago finished with four players in double figures, including Natasha Cloud , who led the team with 16 points. Cloud also had seven assists, four rebounds and a steal.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith calls out ‘classless’ Enes Kanter for agitating WNBA players: ‘You got no business doing that’
articles.summary: Stephen A. Smith recently posed the ridiculous scenario of NBA players transitioning to the WNBA, but even he probably didn’t think Enes Kanter would be desp...
articles.body:
Stephen A. Smith recently posed the ridiculous scenario of NBA players transitioning to the WNBA, but even he probably didn't think Enes Kanter would be desperate enough for attention to accept the challenge.

After recently declaring his eligibility for the 2027 WNBA Draft, Kanter sat courtside during Sunday's Chicago Sky game against the Indiana Fever wearing a shirt that read "Woman" on it . Kanter caught the attention of Sky guard Natasha Cloud , with the former NBA center proceeding to engage by stepping toward the court before being escorted out of the building by security.

"What Enes Kanter did, although he had every right to do it, and although it's clearly to bring attention to the unfairness of not specifically defining what a woman is in a collective bargaining agreement and as a result, somebody who is transgender can wake up and say, 'I'm a female and I want to participate in the NBA' according to the language of the law, you could actually get away with it, and that needs to be clarified," Smith said on his YouTube show.

Right-wing media has celebrated Kanter in recent weeks as the WNBA finds itself at the center of the transgender athlete conversation in the wake of widespread reaction to comments made by Indiana's Sophie Cunningham , who told ESPN she wants to "protect young girls" in sports "against biological men." Smith forecast Kanter's antics several weeks ago on his SiriusXM Radio show, defending Cunningham by noting he doesn't want to see NBA players transition to the WNBA .

But Kanter's faux quest to play professional women's basketball isn't meant to bring attention to the WNBA's collective bargaining agreement, it's meant to bring attention to himself. And while Smith believes Kanter has a point, he also believes the former NBA player has gone about making that point the wrong way.

"Enes Kanter was very wrong," Smith admitted. "It was a classless thing for him to do. Because the ladies that are playing don't have anything to do with this. The league does, it's collective bargaining agreement may…but the actual ladies that are involved, have nothing to do with this and they don't deserve to be agitated the way he was clearly willing to do at the game. It wasn't just about him standing. He was just about to step to her. You got no business doing that. That was excessive."

"Enes Kanter, I believe went too far by showing up in attendance with that shirt on," Smith continued. "Show some class, bro. That's not the ladies that's doing this…Enes Kanter was wrong for being in attendance for that game and being antagonistic to those ladies. They don't deserve that. There's other ways he could have made his message felt. But he's not wrong for illustrating that men don't need to be competing in women's sports."

Kanter is wrong for attempting to make men competing in professional women's basketball out to be a legitimate issue facing the WNBA, when in reality, it's not. His illegitimate attempt at declaring for the WNBA Draft doesn't change the fact that no transgender athlete has attempted to join a WNBA team. This is not an issue the WNBA is facing; it's an issue conservative media is fabricating.
